subject: Vocabulary
topic: Synonyms in Context — Choose the Best Fitting Synonym (W11 B1)

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of FELICITOUS as used in this sentence:
'The speaker made a felicitous remark that perfectly summarised the complex situation.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. FELICITOUS = well-chosen or suited to the circumstances; apt; well-expressed. 'A felicitous remark' = a well-chosen, apt remark. Context clue: 'perfectly summarised the complex situation' confirms it means exactly right/apt. Root: Latin 'felix' = happy/lucky, but in modern usage 'felicitous' means 'well-suited' not just 'happy'. Trap: Unfortunate = the antonym (INfelicitous); Lengthy = not implied; Formal = unrelated meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of TACITURN as used in this sentence:
'He was so taciturn that his colleagues barely knew what he was thinking.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. TACITURN = reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little. Context: colleagues 'barely knew what he was thinking' because he spoke so little. Synonym: RESERVED (not given to sharing thoughts/speaking much). Trap: Talkative = antonym (loquacious is the near-antonym); Energetic = relates to activity, not communication; Sociable = being friendly/outgoing (doesn't mean silent).

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of AMELIORATE as used in this sentence:
'Several measures were taken to ameliorate the living conditions of flood victims.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. AMELIORATE = to make (something bad or unsatisfactory) better; to improve. Context: 'measures taken to ameliorate living conditions' of disaster victims = measures to IMPROVE their living conditions. Trap: Worsen = antonym (exacerbate, aggravate); Investigate = unrelated; Publicise = unrelated. The root: Latin 'melior' = better. Ameliorate is a formal/official register word frequently tested in SSC CGL.

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of VOLUBLE as used in this sentence:
'The voluble spokesperson spoke for nearly an hour without pause.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. VOLUBLE = speaking or spoken incessantly and fluently; talkative. Context: 'spoke for nearly an hour without pause' confirms the meaning of being extremely talkative and fluent. Trap: Silent = antonym (taciturn = silent; voluble = talkative); Aggressive = unrelated to speaking style; Nervous = unrelated to speaking volume/frequency.

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of IMPECUNIOUS as used in this sentence:
'The impecunious student struggled to buy textbooks for the new semester.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. IMPECUNIOUS = having little or no money; poor. Context: 'struggled to buy textbooks' = a financial problem. Synonym: DESTITUTE (having no money). Root: Latin 'pecunia' = money. Closely related: impecuniosity = state of having no money. Trap: Wealthy = antonym; Diligent = relating to effort, not money; Brilliant = relating to intelligence, not financial situation.

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of NEFARIOUS as used in this sentence:
'The gang's nefarious activities included smuggling, extortion, and money laundering.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. NEFARIOUS = (of an action or activity) wicked or criminal. Context: 'smuggling, extortion, and money laundering' are all criminal/wicked activities — these confirm nefarious = wicked. Trap: Charitable = antonym (extremely positive); Secretive = describes secrecy but not wickedness (the activities mentioned are indeed criminal, not just secret); Organised = describes coordination (the gang may be organised, but 'nefarious' refers to moral quality, not organisation).

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of EPHEMERAL as used in this sentence:
'In the digital age, trends are ephemeral — what is popular today may be forgotten tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. EPHEMERAL = lasting for a very short time; transient. Context: 'popular today, forgotten tomorrow' = lasting only briefly. Synonym: TRANSIENT (not permanent, fleeting). Root: Greek 'ephemeros' = lasting only a day (epi = on/upon, hemera = day). Trap: Everlasting = antonym (eternal, permanent); Viral = spreading widely (relates to speed of spread, not duration); Predictable = unrelated to time duration.

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of LOQUACIOUS as used in this sentence:
'The loquacious host kept the audience entertained with a continuous stream of anecdotes.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. LOQUACIOUS = tending to talk a great deal; talkative. Context: 'continuous stream of anecdotes' confirms the host talked a lot. Synonym: GARRULOUS (excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters). Trap: Taciturn = antonym (reserved, says little); Melancholic = sad, gloomy (unrelated to speaking habits); Pedantic = overly concerned with minor academic details (relates to style, not quantity of speech).

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of PERFIDIOUS as used in this sentence:
'The perfidious minister leaked state secrets to the enemy while pretending to serve the nation.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. PERFIDIOUS = deceitful and untrustworthy; guilty of betrayal or treachery. Context: 'leaked secrets while pretending to serve the nation' = a double-dealer/traitor = treacherous. Synonym: TREACHEROUS. Root: Latin 'perfidia' = breach of faith. Trap: Loyal = antonym (the minister was the opposite of loyal); Ambitious = wanting power/success (doesn't imply betrayal); Incompetent = lacking skill (unrelated to betrayal).

questions.stem:
Choose the synonym of OSTENTATIOUS as used in this sentence:
'His ostentatious display of wealth — designer clothes, imported cars, and lavish parties — drew both admiration and envy.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. OSTENTATIOUS = characterised by pretentious or showy display; designed to impress. Context: 'designer clothes, imported cars, and lavish parties' are listed as examples of showy/flashy display. Synonym: SHOWY (attracting attention by being overly elaborate). Trap: Modest = antonym (the opposite of ostentatious); Characteristic = typical of something (unrelated to showiness); Secretive = hiding things (the opposite — ostentatious = making things very visible).
